notes: Category 3 of the taxonomy in docs/pool_edge_plan.md: the interval contains both zero AND the hypothesised effect, so the test said nothing. These are NOT negatives.
The evaluator resolves ~2 ATS points (RWB-15). Most single features are worth a fraction of that, so landing here is the DEFAULT outcome for a real small signal.
Effects are stored so POSITIVE FAVOURS THE CANDIDATE regardless of the metric's own polarity; Brier and MAE must be negated before recording.
A pooled estimate justifies ONE predeclared combined look on a rotation window none of the inputs touched. It is never itself a finding.

ecdf_smoothing_accuracy.classification_evidence: Brier and log-loss improve with high confidence on both leagues (NFL P=1.000, CFB P 0.90-0.96), but forced-pick accuracy is unresolved and leans NEGATIVE on the better-powered CFB instrument (P of improving 0.08-0.13) and is a coin flip on NFL (P 0.25-0.56). Sign recorded as leaning against the candidate; this is a genuine directional bit, not a max over arms. Flips 7.4% of CFB and 7.9% of NFL picks, concentrated 2-3x at |line| < 3.
ecdf_smoothing_accuracy.description: Replacing the discretized ~500-900-draw residual ECDF with a smoothed estimate. Calibration improves; the accuracy question is what is unresolved.
ecdf_smoothing_accuracy.notes: Do not ship on the Brier gain alone -- the project is graded on accuracy and the accuracy sign leans the wrong way. Calibration value belongs to the Best Pick ranker.

fourth_down_aggressiveness.classification_evidence: The completely-unpriced hypothesis is +0.174 pts and sits INSIDE the interval. Resolving it at 95% needs ~24,000 games, about 90 NFL seasons.
fourth_down_aggressiveness.description: Coach go-for-it rate above situational expectation, lagged a season.
fourth_down_aggressiveness.notes: Reliability is measured relative to each season's league norm, which strips the league-wide drift toward going for it; the naive figure is +0.666. The 0.123 EPA-points/game magnitude is a bin-EPA estimate that selection likely inflates.

groupwise_ridge_block_penalties.classification_evidence: Interval contains zero. Recorded rather than discarded per the three-kinds-of-negative rule. THREE caveats that must travel with it: (a) this is the MAX over 22 configurations, so its sign is NOT one clean bit under the null and it must be excluded from any pooled sign test; (b) the accuracy dose-response is non-monotone; (c) the picks it relocates are won at only 50.8% (1,116 of 2,195). The Brier half IS resolved and monotone across the predeclared symmetric grid (market_light_10 +0.000304 [+0.000055, +0.000589], P+ 0.9915), with the block allocation, not the global alpha, as the resolvable half.
groupwise_ridge_block_penalties.description: Per-feature-block ridge penalties (light on market columns, heavy on thin player columns) rather than one global alpha. CFB screen, 11,989 games.
groupwise_ridge_block_penalties.notes: Blocked behind deriving ridge_alpha: at the production alpha=10 the entire block axis is a no-op (median principal direction shrunk 0.27%). Route the Brier gain to the Best Pick ranker, where Brier is the right currency.

hc_year_one_fade.classification_evidence: Era split is the whole question: clean 2009-2017 gap is +0.09 (n=391), mined 2018-2025 gap is -8.08 (n=465). The clean era REFUTES the -8 magnitude but NOT a moderate true effect -- a true -4 sits only 1.43 sigma from the clean-era observation, so it is not excluded. An earlier draft of this session called that a category-2 close; that was wrong and is corrected here. Escapes the closed coach-quality-reputation mechanism (reliability 0.063), which is a claim about a persistent coach TRAIT; this is an event/transition claim needing no stable trait. Not the team-quality ceiling either: invariant to quality by construction, and the gap survives inside the low-quality tercile (45.75% vs 51.46%).
hc_year_one_fade.description: First-year head coaches, weeks 1-8, cover below the kept-coach rate. Reproduced by two independent pipelines: 46.73% year-one vs 50.99% kept-coach on 856 games, gap -4.26 points.
hc_year_one_fade.notes: SCALE: the raw effect is a 4.26-point cover-rate gap on the 783 games (17.7% of the slate) with a first-year coach in weeks 1-8. Recorded on the FULL-SLATE scale so it is commensurable with feature-level accuracy deltas; an un-scaled subset effect would dominate any pool it entered. SIGN: the raw gap is negative (year-one coaches cover less); recorded positive because the registry's sign asks whether the evidence favours the candidate HYPOTHESIS, which was exactly that they underperform. SIGN ORIENTATION: the raw cover-rate gap is -4.26 (year-one coaches cover LESS). Recorded as +4.26 because the registry's sign asks whether the evidence favours the CANDIDATE HYPOTHESIS, and the hypothesis was exactly that they underperform -- the edge is exploitable by fading them. injury_value_lost_gradient.classification_evidence: Unchanged headline: the disagreement statistic resolves (rank-biserial +0.248 [+0.046,+0.450], p=0.016) but the ACCURACY effect does not (+1.75 [-0.69,+4.27], P+ 0.899) on the already-spent [2020, 2021] window, 456 games. NEW this session (docs/injury_value_lost.md): (1) split-half reliability of the underlying value-lost signal, measured on the full 2009-2025 history (4,431 games, 384 team-seasons, temporal odd/even-week split) is Pearson r=0.874 [0.843,0.901], Spearman-Brown corrected full-length reliability=0.933 [0.915,0.948], P+=1.000 (4000/4000 bootstrap draws) -- rules out 'refuted: no split-half reliability' per AGENTS.md. (2) The RAPM-participation value-lost construct (M6, the family's one same-kind negative, -0.43 pts) has EQUALLY high reliability (0.860 raw / 0.925 corrected) -- so reliability does NOT explain M6's negative sign; more likely M6 tests the marginal value of a second, QB-inclusive, correlated value-lost construct stacked on top of one already in the model (full_player_participation = full_player_value + participation family), not whether value-lost as a concept works. (3) The mechanism-screen result survives a market-line-movement control unchanged (value_magnitude vs |close-open| line move: Pearson 0.029, near-zero; residualized disagreement rank-biserial 0.249 [0.047,0.451] p=0.016, statistically identical to the raw 0.248). (4) Survives dropping every QB-involved game: on the 397/456 games (87%) where neither presumed starter carried any listed injury, rank-biserial is still positive (+0.188 [-0.027,0.403], p=0.086) at comparable magnitude to the full sample -- consistent with the structural code finding that injury_skill_epa_value_lost deliberately zeroes QB rushing/receiving production (players.py:1260-1283), so this is provably not a QB proxy. (5) A methodologically CLEANER isolation exists and was run for the first time: player_value profile on game_features_player_value.parquet (built with FIXED-prior severity per its manifest player_feature_version=v2 tag, confirmed NOT learned) contrasted against the player baseline differs by ONLY the two value-lost columns -- zero semantics-shift confound, unlike this entry's original B-A contrast which mixed learned-severity semantics_shift into the same delta. That clean contrast gives +1.316 pts [-0.460,+3.247], P+ 0.8875, on the same 456 games, 26 disagreements (61.5% candidate win rate) -- smaller than +1.75 (removing the confound costs about a third of a point) but directionally intact. Recommend citing +1.316/P+0.8875 as the number to predeclare a narrowed family against, not the conflated +1.75 recorded here.
injury_value_lost_gradient.description: The availability/player-value half of the MOD-07 stack, whose gain concentrates in games with more injury VALUE lost rather than more availability-RATE shift. Tercile accuracy by value lost is monotone: -0.66 / +0.66 / +5.26 points.
injury_value_lost_gradient.notes: The narrowed candidate worth building: value-weighted injury magnitude with the learned-rate half dropped -- confirmed in docs/injury_value_lost.md section 4 using game_features_player_value.parquet (fixed severity) rather than the weak_stack table (learned severity), which removes the semantics-shift confound entirely. Predeclare as a new family `injury_value_lost_narrowed` inheriting mod07_weak_signal_stack (contaminates [2020,2021]); earliest eligible block after inherited contamination is [2022, 2023], one of only two remaining full opener blocks in the 2020-2025 pool. Do not assign until the 2026 prospective mod07_weak_signal_stack challenger (already ACTIVE_PROSPECTIVE, artifacts/prospective/challengers.json) has produced its own number -- docs/injury_value_lost.md section 7 has the full predeclaration text to freeze verbatim. CFB cannot screen this family: value_lost requires a pregame injury-severity signal and none exists in any CFB source (docs/cfb_data.md, 'Availability semantics (fail closed)'); the nearest feasible CFB proxy (realized participation continuity, a different, postgame construct) already ran and lost (-0.67 pts on 8,933 games, cfb_role_continuity family, closed_negative).

penalty_discipline.classification_evidence: A 0.67-point quartile gap (49.85% vs 50.52%) on quartile-sized samples cannot separate 'priced' from 'too small to see'.
penalty_discipline.description: Team penalty rate, quartile split against the market.
penalty_discipline.notes: Scale corrected 2026-08-17: was recorded as 0.0067 (a fraction) while fourth_down_aggressiveness used points, which would have made any pool of the two silently meaningless. accuracy_points are PERCENTAGE POINTS. Still carries no interval, so it cannot be pooled until re-measured with one.

player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.classification_evidence: Reclassified 2026-08-18. The two arms differ only in ridge alpha (1 vs 10), which shrinks the median principal direction of the active-model design by 0.03% vs 0.27% -- a near-null contrast by construction (docs/groupwise_ridge.md). The +-1.1033 pair is therefore a calibration of how much accuracy this evaluator manufactures from nothing on 997 games (coin-flip sd ~1.58 points), not a measurement of QB continuity. No sample size rescues a null contrast, so it is a refuted mechanism rather than an unresolved signal, and it must not be pooled or counted as a sign-test bit.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.description: QB + lineup continuity features, compared at MATCHED regularization rather than against a baseline at a different ridge alpha.
player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.notes: The window [2014, 2017] is SPENT and must never be re-scored -- this entry records a re-reading of what was already measured, not a new look. The deployable question ('is this configuration better than the frozen one?') was answered honestly as no; the family question ('do these features carry signal?') was not answered at all and should never have been described as closed. Actionable reading: the features want less regularization than the rest of the design, and a single global alpha cannot give them that -- group-wise ridge penalties are the mechanism this implies.

residual_location_recency_hl200_cfb.classification_evidence: Resolvably WRONG SIGN: season-blocked interval excludes zero below (P+ 0.014) and Brier resolves negative at P+ 0.000. Wrong sign with a demonstrably sensitive instrument is a refuted mechanism per AGENTS.md, not a below-power null.

ridge_alpha_global.classification_evidence: Week-blocked interval contains zero (P+ 0.758); season-blocked P+ 0.703, also unresolved. This is a SECOND LOOK: alpha=2,500 was chosen after a coarse 13-point predeclared grid (1e-3..1e5) showed the Brier curve turning over near 1,000-3,000, then a 6-point refinement grid localized the minimum. The refinement narrows a point estimate; it does not license a stronger claim than the coarse grid already supports (coarse alpha=3,000: accuracy +0.213 pts, P+ 0.716/0.659; Brier +0.000294, P+ 0.933/0.894). The Brier half IS resolved and consistent across the whole 300-10,000 band (all P+ >= 0.75, most >= 0.93), which is the resolvable companion result -- see notes.
ridge_alpha_global.description: Global ridge penalty (market_residual / weak_stack, CFB walk-forward screen, 2,000-alpha grid) vs the frozen production alpha=10. Brier/log-loss improve with high confidence in a broad 300-10,000 band (peak near 2,000-2,500); forced-pick accuracy does not move.
ridge_alpha_global.notes: Blocked behind: the active production model runs alpha=10, which shrinks the median principal direction of the fitted design by only 0.27% (docs/ridge_alpha.md sec 1) -- i.e. alpha does essentially nothing on the ~70 well-conditioned, signal-bearing directions and is not chosen with any bias-variance tradeoff in mind. Accuracy is flat across [0.001, 10000], a 7-order-of-magnitude range, with no candidate clearing P+ >= 0.90 on both week- and season-blocking. Route the Brier gain to the Best Pick ranker (docs/pool_edge_plan.md queue item 2), not to a production accuracy swap. Do not pool this with groupwise_ridge_block_penalties without checking commensurability -- different mechanism (global penalty level vs. per-block allocation), though both are ridge-penalty-structure findings on the same CFB instrument with the same accuracy/Brier split pattern.
